correctness.rationale: For any finite loopless quiver Q over F_q, with parallel arrows and cycles allowed but J^2=0, x=sum_v a_v e_v+sum_e x_e alpha_e gives [x,y]_e=(a_s-a_t)y_e-(b_s-b_t)x_e. Nonmonochromatic edge rows are independent pivots. On monochromatic E_a and support S={e in E_a:x_e!=0}, the remaining oriented incidence map has rank n-k(S) in any field, including characteristic 2 and multigraphs. Thus rank ad_x=m-|E_a|+n-k(S), and counting x yields formula (1); maximizing rank gives m-delta_q(G), with delta=0 iff a q-coloring has monochromatic induced forests, equivalent to vertex arboricity <=q for simple graphs. Summing kernel sizes and reversing sums gives commuting-pair count q^m sum_{S subset E}(q-1)^|S| q^{2k(S)}. Independently enumerated formula histograms on several F2/F3 graphs including full K5 distribution [2,20,110,460,1616,960,4320,11200,8960,5120], and reconstructed Git source tree. Orientation independence concerns rank/cardinality distributions, not identities of centralizer subrings.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge O PASS for the all-loopless-quiver adjoint-rank distribution plus sharp vertex-arboricity criterion and random-cluster commuting specialization. The Fortuin–Kasteleyn/Tutte sum is a classical graph polynomial and not separately novel; a published finite Kronecker path algebra record establishes the two-vertex parallel-arrow special case. The inspected Green–Schroll 'commuting algebra' is a quotient by parallel-path relations, not a theorem on element commutators in F_qQ/J^2. Generic incidence-matrix and coloring facts are known premises. The all-quiver probability formula could be deduced from general class-two algebra/graph methods not located in targeted searches.
